title: FLORA SCHOOL BOARD MEETING
full_story:
The Flora School District met in regular session Monday night renewing their SIJHSAA and IESA memberships and a approving a Holiday World trip for the JR High Band.

They also approved the tentative amended 2025-2026 budget and set June 15th during the regular Board meeting as the date and time for the budget hearing.  Approved the handbook changes and substitute pay and official pay for 2026-2027.  Superintendent Joel Hackney provided an update on committee meetings, provided an update on the progress towards district goals, updated the status of current projects, and provided highlights of summer/future projects.

In personnel matters board members employed Kelli Bernahl as an elementary teacher, Lindy Burkett as a special education teacher, Mollie McNeely as an elementary teacher, and Lacy Althoff as elementary assistant principal for the 2026-2027 school year.

Resignations were accepted from Emma Kitley as paraprofessional, Jim Earleywine as 7th grade volleyball coach, Felicia Fopay as FHS basketball cheerleading sponsor, Lori Shehorn as part-time special education teacher, Samantha Mosbarger as paraprofessional, Alex Beckham as Physical Education/Health Teacher, and Natalie Kizzire as Pre-K PI Supervisor.

They also approved the unpaid medical leave for Danielle Sturm effective April 24th, and the leave of absence submitted by Emma Taylor from August through November 15.

title: OCC SPRING CONCERT
full_story:
The Olney Central College Music Department will present its Spring Concert at 7 pm tonight in the Dr. John D. Stull Performing Arts Center.

The evening will feature performances by the OCC Community Concert Band and Jazz Combo, under the direction of OCC Interim Director of Bands Jena Combs.  Joining them as a special guest will be the Flora High School Band, directed by OCC alumnus Ethan Steber.

Combs is excited to include the high school students in the event, an idea that grew out of a conversation with Steber.

“We were talking about ways to get the community more involved, and the idea came up to invite high school bands to perform with us and feature them in a concert,” she said.  “Ethan immediately volunteered his band to be the first.  We thought it was a cool way to get people here and a great way to help with recruitment.”

Combs previously served as FHS band director before accepting a position at Lincoln Trail College in 2024 and assisting with OCC’s instrumental program this year.  Steber completed his student teaching under Combs and later succeeded her as Flora band director.

The FHS band will present The Great Rubber Chicken Galop by Randall Standridge, American Riversongs by Pierre LaPlante and The Pines of Rome by Ottorino Respighi and arranged by James Curnow.

The high school students will then have an opportunity to perform with the OCC Community Concert Band and the OCC Jazz Combo as the three ensembles come together for the selection Shine on Me by Seattle-based composer and conductor Erin Keeton-Howard.

The OCC Community Concert Band, which brings together OCC students and area musicians, will perform Prestissimo by march-music composer Karl L. King with the arrangement by James Swearingen, Secret Valley by Michael Sweeney and Amazing Grace by Frank Ticheli, whose many works have become standards in concert band repertoire.  Other pieces will include Nevermore and Reverberations by contemporary American composer, conductor and music educator Brian Balmages and Insurrection by composer Gary P. Gilroy.

Selections by the OCC Jazz Combo will include C Jam Blues by legendary jazz performer Duke Ellington and Someone to Watch Over Me by groundbreaking American composer and pianist George Gershwin.  Other pieces include Sonnymoon for Two by jazz saxophonist Sonny Rollins, Brasilian Skies by Masayoshi Takanaka and the Latin-rock hit Oye Como Va by Santana.

Combs invites the community to come out and enjoy this final instrumental performance of the semester.  Admission is a free-will donation.

title: EVACUATION DRILL
full_story:
On the heels of the Anhydrous Ammonia traffic accident that caused Johnsonville Grade School to be evacuated last week, the Clay County Sheriff’s office will be conducting an evacuation drill at Clay City Schools tomorrow.  The drill, which will include Clay City’s Volunteer Fire Department, takes place at 1:00 pm.

Drills of this kind are important when last Tuesday’s accident in Johnsonville is considered.  It was about two and half years ago when, on September 29, 2023 on U.S. Route 40 near Teutopolis a traffic accident resulted in the release of 4,000 gallons of Anhydrous Ammonia into the damp evening air that formed a toxic cloud that claimed the lives of five people in the immediate area and injured 14 others including first responders.

title: ARREST IN SUNDAY SHOOTING
full_story:
An arrest warrant was issued for the arrest of a 21-year-old Centralia man in connection with the fatal Sunday afternoon shooting in Centralia.  Shavonte Samuels turned himself in at the Centralia Police station on Tuesday shortly after the warrant was issued.  Samuels was transported to the Marion County Jail where he is being held on the charge of aggravated discharge of a firearm.

Marion County State’s Attorney Tim Hudspeth said Samuels is one of two persons being sought who are believed to have had a gun at the time of the shooting.  The other person and a third person that was present but not believed to have been armed are still being sought.

State Police announced Monday that a 19-year-old man died from gunshot wounds after being taken to St. Mary’s Hospital following the shooting.  His name has not been released.  They indicated three others were treated and released from the hospital.

title: PLANTING RAPIDLY PROGRESSING
full_story:
Corn and soybean planting continues at a rapid pace in southern Illinois, pushing statewide progress ahead of average.  Statewide, the USDA says 13% of the corn crop is planted, up 9% from last week with 3% emerged, while 20% of soybeans are planted, up 13% from last week.

There were 3.5 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending April 19th.  Statewide, the average temperature was 65.3 degrees, 12.3 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged 1.91 inches, 1.04 inches above normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 6% very short, 16% short, 67% adequate, and 11% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 9% very short, 28% short, 57% adequate, and 6% surplus.

Corn planted reached 13%, compared to the 5-year average of 8%.  Corn emerged reached 3%.

Soybeans planted reached 20%, compared to the 5-year average of 7%.

Winter wheat headed reached 18%, compared to the 5-year average of 6%.  Winter wheat condition was rated 2% very poor, 5% poor, 29% fair, 55% good, and 9% excellent.

title: FARM BILL
full_story:
The House Rules Committee could meet next week to consider the proposed farm bill, according to a committee notice.

The House Ag Committee advanced its version of the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 in early March.  Ag Committee Chair Glenn “GT” Thompson, indicated the legislation has support to make it to a floor vote.

The deadline for members to submit amendments to the farm bill is today (4/22).  The timing of the vote could be pushed due to other legislative debates on funding and reconciliation.

Senate Ag Committee Chair John Boozman, last month said he hoped to begin moving farm bill legislation through his committee within weeks.

title: COOLEST THING IN ILLINOIS
full_story:
Astronauts just returned from their first voyage around the moon since 1972 and a device built by an Illinois company helped fuel the mission’s success.

Created and manufactured in Downers Grove, the NASA Standard Initiator, or NSI, is a small electrically activated pyrotechnic device that initiates propulsion by sparking a chain reaction of heat and pressure in space flight.

“Anytime you have a space launch, anytime you have a separation activity, particularly in space, you need something to push that away and get something to light that initiating event.  And that’s what that device does,” said Steven Hill, president of Chemring Energetic Devices Inc.

Chemring and the NSI won the 2026 “Makers Madness” contest on Wednesday, being named “The Coolest Thing Made in Illinois” for 2026.  The competition is held annually by the Illinois Manufacturers’ Association.

Other finalists for the 2026 competition included; the John Deere Combine, manufactured in East Moline, the Duck Skimmer, a floating weir skimmer used to take the surface layer off the water to remove duck weed, water meal and other pollutants manufactured by Elastec in Carmi, Aerapy PPR HVAC UV System, a system that disinfects the air with ultraviolet light, reducing airborne pathogens, manufactured by Aerapy in St. Charles.

title: STRIKE SETTLED
full_story:
Faculty at the University of Illinois Springfield ended a more than two-week strike on Monday after reaching an agreement with university administrators overnight.

Tenured and tenure-track faculty at UIS, one of three University of Illinois system institutions, went on strike on April 3 after failing to reach an agreement with UIS administrators over pay increases.  The two parties came to an agreement after hours of negotiations on Sunday.

Both sides declined to specify the terms of the agreement until after the UIS United Faculty union could ratify the agreement in the coming days.

It appeared the strike would start having more substantial impacts on students if it continued into another week.  The university sent an email to students on Friday announcing it was prepared to implement a plan this week to help students complete the semester if the strike continued.

The university said alternative plans would be made for students who were not able to complete their assignments because their professors were on strike.  Not all classes at UIS were held up by the strike, however, as many professors are part of a different union.

The union indicated their decision to end the strike was more about ensuring students can complete their classes than any victory in bargaining meetings.

UIS said in a brief statement that it “looks forward to continuing to work together to fulfill its mission to provide a uniquely student-centered educational experience, both in and out of the classroom.”
